quantity: value head, rollout graph replay vs eager forward
rationale: same weights, same inputs, same kernels; only the launch mechanism differs, so any drift at all is a real bug. It came out exactly zero.

quantity: head logits, via the log-prob of a fixed action set
joint log-prob vs sum of 9 Categorical.log_prob
rationale: log_softmax over a -inf-padded row vs 9 separate rows; differs only in reduction order over <=10 elements

quantity: summed entropy vs sum of 9 Categorical.entropy
rationale: pad terms enter as p*log p with p=0, forced to exact zero; the gap is reduction order over <=10 terms

quantity: per-category empirical frequency vs softmax probability
rationale: distribution test, not a numeric one. This is the check that caught the NaN-Gumbel bug; see RNG_PROTOCOL.md.

quantity: relative L2 of the full gradient vector, one step from identical weights, graph vs eager
rationale: the graph is exactly as close to the eager path as the eager path is to itself

quantity: relative L2 of the full gradient vector, fused vs 9-Categorical, both eager
rationale: isolates the sampler change from the graph change; never judged as a compound
exp_avg is a running mean of gradients, so this is a second, multi-step read on gradient equality

quantity: parameter values after K optimizer steps
rationale: REJECTED as a gate. Adam divides by sqrt(v), so a near-zero-gradient parameter turns 1e-07 of fp32 noise into an O(lr) position change; the divergence is chaotic and the control itself moved 3x run to run. A gate whose control moves that much decides nothing. Gradient parity is the claim; the optimizer downstream is stock.
